learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and skills to apply the fundamentals of elasticity and strength of materials to the behavior of real solids.
Knowledge and capacity for the calculation and design of industrial structures and constructions.
General approach to the elastic problem.
Be capable of analyzing and solving technological problems related to elasticity.
Have obtained the ability to write and interpret technical documentation related to elasticity and strength of materials.
Be capable of using the necessary instruments to measure deformations.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Elasticity. Concept of solid. Definition of mechanical prism. Static equilibrium and elastic equilibrium. Stresses derived from the action of a system of forces on a mechanical prism. Concept of stress.

Stress in elastic solids. Concept of stress vector. Intrinsic components of the stress vector. Stresses in a bar subjected to tension. Spherical and cylindrical pressure vessels. Safety coefficients. Stress tensor. Internal forces per unit volume. Equilibrium equations at the boundary. Change of reference system. Principal stresses and directions. Hydrostatic stresses and deviatoric stresses. Stress ellipsoid. Mohr's circle. Maximum tangential stresses.

Deformation in continuous media. Longitudinal deformation. Tangential shear or shear deformation. Displacement field within a solid. Physical interpretation of the components of the strain tensor. Deformation in any direction. Principal directions and invariants. Strain tensor. Relationship between principal stress and strain directions. Volumetric and deviatoric deformation. Compatibility equations. Change of reference system. Mohr's circle in deformations.

Relationship between stresses and strains. Tensile test. Stress-strain curve. Poisson's effect. Shear tests. Constitutive equation of the material. Generalized Hooke's Laws. Lame's equations. Volumetric deformation.

General approach to the elastic problem. Formulation in displacements. Navier's equations. Formulation in stresses. Michel and Beltrami's equations. Strain energy. Energy density. Uniqueness of the solution to the elastic problem. Principle of superposition. Saint-Venant's principle. Thermal stresses and strains. Duhamel's Theorem.

Plane elasticity. Plane stress. Plane strain. Airy's stress function. Characteristic curves of plane elasticity. Two-dimensional problems in polar coordinates. Rotating disk. Solid disk without stresses on its boundary. Disk with a hole of radius "a". Circular tube subjected to pressure. Wedge with a load at the tip. Cylinder subjected to two loads along opposite generators. Indefinite plate with a circular hole. Indefinite plate with a hole subjected to shear stress on its boundary. Indefinite plate with an elliptical hole.

Energy theorems. Elastic energy as a function of applied loads. Influence coefficients. Clapeyron's formulas. Principle of virtual work. Case of a deformable solid. Maxwell-Betti reciprocity theorem. Castigliano's theorems. Menabrea's theorems.
Yield criteria. Tresca's yield criterion. Von Mises' yield criterion. Comparison between Tresca's and Von Mises' yield loci.

Experimental methods in elasticity. Extensiometric method. Electrical strain gauges. Fundamentals and purpose of the photoelastic method. Maxwell's laws. Photoelastic apparatus. Methods for separating principal stresses. Other experimental methods.
assessment_rules: The overall evaluation is based on 100 points. A minimum of 10% of the 20% total for "Theory" is required. A minimum of 31.5% of the 70% total for "Problems" is required; failure to achieve this means failing the course. Practical reports are mandatory, and at least 5% of the 10% corresponding to them must be achieved. The final and extraordinary resit exams consist of a written test with three parts: Theory (20%), Problems (70%), and Practical questions (10%), with the same weighting for each part.
